systems_changed.change_summary: Troopers were walking too slowly in lane; the bug fix restores intended trooper movement speed, so waves arrive, meet and crash on schedule again. This is a regression repair, not a tuning pass — it re-enables normal lane cadence rather than making troopers faster than baseline.
driving_changes: [fix] Fixed bugs that were causing troopers to walk too slowly in lane
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Restores predictable wave timing for last-hits, freeze and push, and re-opens the standard dive/punish windows on an enemy who is stuck under a slow wave. Since the KB says the lead engine sits in the map economy (Tough Crates, Haunt camps, hub fights) rather than the lane, the practical impact is small — it mostly removes an unintended quality-of-life drag on lane phase rather than changing who wins.

tempo_shift.why: Fixing trooper speed only restores baseline lane tempo; it adds no new early snowball or comeback lever, and the KB lead engine (map economy, no comeback valve) is untouched. Faintly toward tempo at best, because normal wave timing makes lane pressure and crashes land as designed again.

archetype_effects.why: On-schedule trooper speed restores the wave-crash timing that makes bullying and dive-punish windows land reliably.
Reliable trooper pathing makes pushed waves and side-lane pressure convert at the intended cadence rather than stalling.
No economy, comeback or objective change accompanies the fix; the Broker stall window and trimmed comeback bounties are unchanged.

intent_read: Valve appears to be patching a regression from the City Never Sleeps map/trooper rework, not steering the meta. The intent is to make lane phase behave as originally designed; the game's lead engine (map economy, no comeback valve) is deliberately left untouched.
